newsitem.title: KENYA: Plot to kill Burundi's Buyoya foiled - regime.
newsitem.headline: Plot to kill Burundi's Buyoya foiled - regime.

text.p: Five people have been arrested in the Burundian capital Bujumbura after authorities foiled an attempt to assassinate military leader Pierre Buyoya, a spokesman for Buyoya said on Wednesday.
"There was an assassination plot to try to confuse the people...The plot has been foiled and five people were apprehended earlier last night (Tuesday)," spokesman Jean-Luc Ndizeye told Reuters.
"The plot was close to coming to fruition and everything had been put in place. Had they not been apprehended they could have carried out the plot within hours not days," he said.
Interior Minister Lieutenant-Colonel Epitace Bayaganakandi announced the plot on Burundian radio on Wednesday and called for calm, Ndizeye said.

"The Ministry of the Interior and Public Security informs the national and international public that security services have just foiled a plot against the life of the head of state," Bayaganakandi said in an address on state-run Radio Burundi monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Two of those arrested were army officers, two were civilians and one was a non-Burundian, Ndizeye said. He added they were all being interrogated. There were few further details.
Two main groups oppose Buyoya's rule -- Hutu rebels fighting a vicious civil war against the army, and Tutsi extremists under ex-president Jean-Baptiste Bagaza who have strong links in the army.
Meanwhile a Burundian doctor was killed in one of three mine explosions to go off in Bujumbura on Wednesday evening, Ndizeye said.
"The entire security forces are trying to make sure the city is secured," he said.
Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army took power in a coup last July, installing ethnic-Tutsi Buyoya and ousting a freely elected Hutu government.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi shortly after the coup demanding unconditional talks between the government and rebels.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since the country's first freely elected president was murdered in an attempted army coup in October 1993.
